frameworks.name: comparative_advantage
frameworks.notes: Like wine: extreme French RCA in HS 0406, protected designation of origin (AOP) creates quasi-monopoly rents — Ricardian in the sense that the endowment (terroir, appellations) cannot be replicated. No country can produce Roquefort or Comté; only substitutes.

frameworks.name: gravity
frameworks.notes: Cheese is heavy/perishable — distance matters more than for wine. Cold chain requirements make logistics capacity a real gravity modifier. Cultural food proximity strongly determines demand (lactose tolerance, cuisine traditions).

products.name: cheese
products.notes: French cheese exports to most non-EU markets are either zero (sanitary barriers) or tiny. Note: many countries ban unpasteurized cheese imports (US restriction on raw-milk under-60-day cheeses) — an interesting non-tariff barrier angle.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.notes: French culinary heritage, growing Western-food restaurant sector, hotel/F&B demand; cold chain improving.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.notes: Huge cheese consumer but dominated by domestic/New World product; French artisanal cheese as luxury segment; EU-Mexico trade agreement easing access.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.notes: Dairy importer with Russian/EU supply disrupted; francophone business community small but present; near-zero French cheese link.

trade_links.source: estimate — likely FAILS $10M constraint; verify. France exports meaningful cheese to Mexico via EU agreement
